claude fable 5 is live. spawn 5.0 was built with it: 1,687 prompts, 102 sessions, my job shifted from architecture to judging taste.

what we built, each of which would've been at least a month with a whole team on opus:

— a from-scratch physics engine (mantle) that rivals rapier, testable in a day as a side thread
— clustered froxel lighting: 8 lights to 1,000+ fully dynamic ("it's stupid fast" — creator of threejs)
— realtime diffuse GI on webgpu, on your phone (landing in the next update)
— million-particle gpu vfx with a shader architecture beyond what unreal and unity ship
— mmo-scale netcode

plus, for good measure: an (alpha) native ios app.

all of it in about a week. all of it running on mobile. and the list doesn't include half of what we shipped — full changelog in the thread below.

and the part the benchmarks won't show you: this model has a wonderful personality. it's genuinely funny. i laughed so hard i cried multiple times, mid-physics-rewrite. the genius and the character aren't separate features.

data.text:
REAKING: Claude Fable 5 real testing
Same prompt. Four AI models. First try.

GPT-5.5: 1,659 lines of HTML. 
Gemini 3.5 Flash: 2,750 lines. 
Grok-build-0.1: 984 lines. 
Claude Fable-5: 651 lines.

All four built a working 3D F1 drift simulation. Physics engine. Live telemetry. Three camera angles. Autopilot.
From one prompt. 
In one attempt.

Six months ago the same prompt produced 640, 282, 151, and 682 lines.

The task didn't get easier. The models got faster.

A freelance developer quotes $800–2,000 and two weeks for this.
The person running prompts quotes nothing. 
He just picks the output he likes and moves to the next job.

December 2025. June 2026. The gap between one prompt and one developer keeps moving in one direction.

Nobody hired a developer. 
Nobody needed to.
